claims.text: Algorithmic decision making in machine learning can be inherently prone to unfairness even without explicit intent.
Fairness-enhancing mechanisms in machine learning can be categorized into pre-process, in-process, and post-process mechanisms.

evidence.description: Recent studies have shown that algorithmic decision making may be inherently prone to unfairness, even when there is no intention for it.
Fairness-enhancing mechanisms are then reviewed and divided into pre-process, in-process, and post-process mechanisms.

methodologies.name: Literature Review and Categorical Framework Analysis
methodologies.description: A comprehensive review and taxonomy of algorithmic bias sources, fairness metrics, and fairness-enhancing mechanisms primarily centered on classification tasks.

limitations.text: Algorithmic decision-making systems in machine learning are inherently prone to unfairness.
Existing research and fairness mechanisms focus primarily on classification tasks.

future_work.text: Development and evaluation of algorithmic fairness mechanisms for machine learning tasks beyond classification.
